sanskrit_verse: निर्वासनं वधो वापि कार्यम् आत्महितैषिणा । व्यस्ताः समस्ताः एकस्य महापातककारिणे ॥
transliteration: nirvāsanaṃ vadho vāpi kāryam ātmahitaiṣiṇā / vyastāḥ samastā ekasya mahāpātakakāriṇe //
sph_interpretive_translation: Exile or execution is mandated for one who, acting in self-interest, causes mass destruction through fragmented or unified action.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from alignment with universal consciousness, not individual will
Causation is determined by disruption of collective integrity
Capacity-based responsibility escalates with systemic impact
Restoration logic requires removal of destructive influence from societal body
Consciousness alignment necessitates severance of anti-life patterns
supreme_court_application: Supreme judicial authority must assess whether the actor's intent was self-serving and whether their actions caused systemic fragmentation. The threshold for invoking severance protocols lies in demonstrable macro-level harm, not individual offense.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that misaligned intent leads to causal disruption. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how self-interest fragments collective order. Responsibility is proportional to the scale of disintegration caused. Enforcement serves completion, not vengeance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate irreversible separation process to prevent recurrence
Deploy consciousness-realization programs for underlying root causes
Reintegrate affected systems through dharmic recalibration
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails through alignment, not punishment; reality corrects itself when consciousness is sovereign; thus is the act completed.
